query: When a business closes valuable customers but does not generate enough qualified sales conversations, how should it diagnose whether the failing part is the attraction offer/customer acquisition offer versus the upsell, downsell, or continuity, and which offer-stack function should be addressed first?

## [§2.2.e] The four offer types — Attraction, Upsell, Downsell, Continuity

So now let's talk about all the things that I just did, but we're gonna chunk up so that you can apply it to any business. All right? So there's attraction offers, upsell offers, downsell offers and continuity offers. The objective of each of these. Attraction offers is to liquidate how much it costs you to cus- get a customer. Upsell offers are to maximize profit. Downsell offers are to maximize conversion. Continuity offers are to stabilize cash flow in the business. There are many ways to accomplish CFA. Some businesses can do it with only one offer. Some businesses get funding so they don't need to break even to get customers 'cause they have outside money that's injected into their system. But for everyone else probably watching this, I will explain a model that I have seen emerge over and over and over again within the businesses that I built. So when I look at every single amazing business that I've built that's made a lot of money, they had these things pretty much in this sequence. And it doesn't happen all at once. It just often becomes something that you build towards. So to be very clear, I'm not saying you start with a fully fledged money model, 'cause it will break your b- whole business in half. You wanna start with one, you start adding in layers, like layers of paint. You just keep putting more and more layers on it. And so again, you can build an amazing business with just one or two of these things. And sometimes it's worth keeping it simple and just doing that. If you can scale with... I wanna scale with as few offers as humanly possible. But I still wanna maximize how much money I make in the shortest period of time. So if I have to add more, I will, to enable me scaling. But I wanna have as few as I can, 'cause I wanna have as little operational drag as possible. All right? And so it has four prongs or four different vectors and different offers that correspond to each objective. All right? So this beautiful little image took me a very long time to figure out. Right? And so we have attraction offers that bring people in the door. We have upsell offers that typically happen immediately after that get people to buy more stuff. We have downsell offers for people who, who don't say yes to either of these things, so we can still get conversions and then potentially upsell them later. And then we have continuity offers on the back, which get them into a recurring cash flow payment to the business. And so let's explain how they all work together to make a symphony of CFA. All right. So here, we turn strangers into customers, get, come spend more money. Lower CAC is to get people... Excuse me, is to get people to say yes when they would have said no, which is what you offer when they say no. And then with continuity, you keep people buying. All right? Which is meaning you get them to buy again. All right? So those are the four prongs.

source_material.text: So we just finished the downsell offer section, and now we move on, to the magic of continuity offers. I've been a continuity guy my whole life, and so this is a section that I hold near and dear to my heart. It has made me a tremendous amount of money. It also stabilizes cash flow for the business. And so in our four money. models, we have attraction, upsells, down sells, and now, kaboom, continuity. So continuity. offers provide ongoing value that customers make ongoing payments for until they cancel. They boost the profit from every customer and give you one last thing to sell. Continuity offers are awesome because you sell. once and get paid again, and again, and again. So here's my quick explanation. Let's say you offer something for $1,000 to 100 people and 10 people buy. You make $10,000. 10 times $1,000. Okay. Now, let's say that you talk to the same 100 people, but you make your $1,000 thing $50 a month instead. And at 50 bucks, we can get 40 out of the 100 to buy. Ð¸. And if you keep those people, for 20 months, you still make $1,000 from each customer. So you go from making $10,000 now and zero dollars over time to $2,000 now and $40,000 over time. And as an added bonus, in the first example, if you only sold 10 customers, you'd only have 10 customers to upsell later. If you use a continuity offer and sold 40 customers, you'd have four times the customers to upsell later, which is a massive difference. This is fundamentally why people do continuity. You can sell more people at a lower price, you can still collect the same LTV, and you get four times the customers to upsell later. The pros are you can attract more customers compared to something more expensive. The cons are but you make way less money now, which makes it tough to use as an attraction offer on its own, which is why we put it last, or at least why I tend to put it last. So the TL;DR is that by making continuity offers last, we get the best of all worlds. We get cash today from attraction offers, upsell offers, and downsell offers, and we get a little cash today and tons of cash tomorrow from continuity offers. Note, to be clear, you can make continuity offers whenever and however you want. There are no rules, all right? They can attract new customers, upsell and downsell current customers, or reengage old customers, same as all the others.
